reason_for_new_generation: Gen-1 failed Golden Axe III: structural lift was positive but nonsignificant and mean best-Maeda-minus-best-non-Maeda margin was negative. Post-failure diagnostics showed pitch/interval signal but rhythm dilution and persistent physical-channel ambiguity.
target_access_rule: Sonic 3 remains excluded until the Gen-2 validation gates pass. Golden Axe III may not be used again to tune this frozen candidate after Sonic 3D structural validation begins.

primary_representation.event_source: ordinary full YM2612 key-ons using the same DAC and CH3-special exclusions as Gen-1
primary_representation.part_definition: one active physical YM2612 channel with at least two ordinary full-FM key-ons
part_features: relative_semitone_interval_histogram clipped to <-24 and >24 exactly as Gen-1
primary_representation.part_correspondence: maximum-weight one-to-one bipartite assignment across active channels
primary_representation.track_similarity: arithmetic mean of the matched part similarities
primary_representation.weight_selection: The 0.5/0.5 weighting is intentionally untuned. Exploratory Golden Axe sweeps showed other weights, including pure bigrams, could score slightly better; those are rejected to avoid selecting the numerical optimum on the development world.

development_result.interpretation: The untuned part matcher repairs the aggregate Gen-1 development failure, including flipping mean separation margin positive. This is development evidence only, not validation.

no_rescue_rules: Do not change the 0.5/0.5 weights after viewing Sonic 3D features.
Do not add rhythm, contour, patch, realization, or an unmatched-part penalty to rescue a failed validation.
Do not remove Sonic 3D singleton sentinels or difficult queries post hoc.
A failed validation requires a Gen-3 preregistration before further model changes.
Similarity can support only a calibrated candidate statement, never historical authorship by itself.
